title_eng: Transformer-Based Early Detection of Sepsis from Intensive Care Unit Multivariate Time Series Data
abstract:
Abstract— This study proposes a Transformer-based model 
for early sepsis prediction using multivariate time-series data 
from approximately 40,000 patients, achieving a receiver 
operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.949 and an area 
under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.379. 
Clinical Relevance— This study explores the application of a 
Transformer-based model designed to capture longitudinal 
physiological patterns for sepsis detection. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction with high 
mortality worldwide (40~70%) [1]. Early suspicion and timely 
intervention are critical for improving septic patients’ survival. 
In this study, we apply a multivariate time-series Transformer 
model (MTS-TR) [2] to early sepsis prediction and investigate 
whether explicitly modeling temporal dependencies can 
improve predictive performance. 
II. METHODS 
The data used in this study were obtained from the 2019 
PhysioNet Challenge and were collected from the intensive 
care units of two institutions: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical 
Center (Set A) and Emory University Hospital (Set B) [3]. Set 
A (20,336 patients) was used for training and Set B (20,000 
patients) for evaluation. Each patient record includes six 
demographic variables, eight vital signs, and twenty -six 
clinical laboratory measurements, with both the data and 
sepsis labels recorded at hourly intervals [3]. Labels were 
defined for six-hour-ahead sepsis prediction: time points 
within six hours prior to sepsis onset were labeled as 1, earlier 
pre-onset points and all non-sepsis cases were labeled as 0. 
The model architecture comprises a Transformer encoder 
and a classification layer. Missing values were median- 
imputed, and variable-length sequences were zero-padded to a 
length of 336 and masked, with padding points labeled to 
−100 and excluded from training and evaluation. Temporal 
variability in vital signs was encoded using 12-hour window 
statistics (median, max, min, and max-min). Differences 
relative to prior observations, and normalized change rates for 
eight vital signs were also included. In total, 116 features were 
provided as input. Missing values that occurred during feature 
calculation were filled with −999 and masked during training 
(Anaconda, Python 3.10.16, Torch 2.5.1+cu118).

III. RESULTS 
 The proposed model achieved an area under the receiver 
operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.949, an area 
under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.379 for six- 
hour-ahead sepsis prediction (Fig.1). Table 1 compares our 
model with previously reported studies from the 2019 
PhysioNet Challenge that provided AUROC results. However, 
direct comparison is limited due to unreported metrics and the 
challenge utility score [3].

Spe: specificity; F1: F1 score; MTS-TR: Multi-variate time series transformer; GBM: gradient boosting machine; EoXGB: ensemble of 
XGBoost; LSTM: long short term memory; TR: transformer; AE: Auto encoder; RF: random forest. 
IV. DISCUSSION & CONCLUSION 
Our results indicate that self-attention-based Transformers 
can effectively model temporal dependencies in multivariate 
clinical time-series data, yielding improved predictive 
performance. This supports the broader applicability of 
Transformer architectures to time-series clinical prediction 
tasks. Future work will investigate interpretability via 
DeepSHAP and evaluate generalizability on external 
datasets.
